newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end flat, big buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end flat, big buyers sidelined.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed flat on Monday, with interest limited to a handful of shares, brokers said.
Wall Street's climb to record levels had little impact on the largely insulated Colombo bourse, where the all share index ended 0.23 points higher at 562.26.
"Activity was curtailed to retail buying because there are no big quantities of shares for bigger buyers," said Buddhike Payoe of Lanka Securities.
Blue chip Development Finance Corp of Ceylon led the rise, gaining two rupees to 265. Ceylon brewery rose one rupee to 32.

Turnover totalled only 4.92 million rupees against last month's daily average of about 15 million. Among actives were Kelani Valley Plantations, which rose 75 cents to 21 rupees, and Dockyard which traded unchanged at 11 rupees.
Trading in Ceylon Oxygen Co resumed after the stock exchange suspended it on September 11, when the company announced a rights issue at a premium to the current market price.

Ceylon Oxygen offered a one-for-two rights issue at 60 rupees against the last traded price of 47.50. Brokers said buyers quoted Ceylon Oxygen at 46 rupees but there were no sell offers. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
